headline: Democrats flip Congress, Trump reshuffles the White House, and Canada's job losses mount
summary: Democrats won control of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms and Trump responded by naming Stephen Miller chief of staff. In Canada, Ottawa tabled its budget as unemployment rose to 6.7%, while the Iran war and tariffs kept pressure on prices and trade.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up
top.what: Democrats flipped Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms, with projections of at least 259 House and 54 Senate seats and the Alaska and Mississippi races still unresolved.
top.why: It reshapes U.S. policy on tariffs and investigations, which matters to Canadian exporters.

top.headline: Trump says U.S. may have to 'destroy' rest of Iran as war shadows post-midterm politics
top.what: The Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption continued, with Trump suggesting the U.S. may have to 'destroy' the rest of Iran.
top.why: The conflict drives oil prices and gas costs in Ontario.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue and Democrats say they would seek to repeal them.
top.why: Tariffs hit Ontario manufacturing jobs and prices.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October and unemployment rose to 6.7%, after bigger losses in August and September.
top.why: It shapes Bank of Canada rate decisions and job security for Ontarians.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: Ottawa's second Carney budget projects a $62.3B deficit and holds immigration levels mostly steady.
top.why: It sets federal spending, taxes and housing priorities for years.

top.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
top.what: Trump named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, effective Nov. 9, replacing Susie Wiles.
top.why: It signals a harder line on immigration and Democrats after the midterm losses.

top.headline: Trump says he was 'a little bit surprised' by losses, warns of vetoes
top.what: Trump said he was surprised by the losses and warned he would use vetoes; Speaker Johnson is stepping aside as GOP leader.
top.why: It frames the fight over tariffs and investigations in 2027.

top.headline: With a $1.12-billion budget shortfall looming, Ford rules out a 'new deal' 2.0 for Toronto
top.what: Toronto faces a $1.12B shortfall and Premier Ford ruled out a new deal for the city.
top.why: It raises the risk of higher property taxes or service cuts in Toronto.
